messages.author: 4452cc54e2894e45
messages.subject: Extracting standard errors from occu()
parts:
Happy holidays everyone,

I am running a series of simulations where I want to extract various outputs from a few thousand model runs. For example:

> out_test <- occu(formula = ~ bait ~ PC1, data = test)
> summary(out_test)

is working as expected and I'm able to access the AIC and parameter estimates as follows:

> out_test@AIC   
> out_test@estimates@estimates$det      # table of estimates, SE, z, P|z| for detection
> out_test@estimates@estimates$state  # table ... for occupancy
> out_test@estimates@estimates$state@estimates   # mean estimates

However, I have not had any success accessing the standard errors, z values, or p-values associated with the @estimates tables. When I look at the structure of the tables there does not appear to be any slot where this information exist:

> str(out_test@estimates@estimates$state)
> showClass("unmarkedEstimate")

I suspect this has something to do with unmarked being an S4 class (?) but that is where my experience hits a brick wall. Is there a way to extract the standard errors, z values, and p-values from an unmarkedEstimate class object?

Best,
-ph

_________________
Philip DeWitt
Wildlife Ecologist
Ontario, Canada

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Extracting standard errors from occu()
parts:
The easiest way is probably to use summary(), which in addition to printing them also returns a data frame of these stats:

s <- summary(out_test)

s$state[,4] # p value

Ken

messages.author: 4452cc54e2894e45
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Extracting standard errors from occu()
parts:
Thanks Ken,

Works like a charm! This is much easier than searching around inside the structure of the object. The fact that this outputs a named list of dataframes makes this particularly appealing:

> str(s)
List of 2
 $ state:'data.frame': 2 obs. of  4 variables:
  ..$ Estimate: num [1:2] 6.8 107.9
  ..$ SE      : num [1:2] 2.01 30.25
  ..$ z       : num [1:2] 3.39 3.57
  ..$ P(>|z|) : num [1:2] 0.000709 0.000361
 $ det  :'data.frame': 2 obs. of  4 variables:
  ..$ Estimate: num [1:2] -1.0306 -0.0912
  ..$ SE      : num [1:2] 0.2046 0.0595
  ..$ z       : num [1:2] -5.04 -1.53
  ..$ P(>|z|) : num [1:2] 4.75e-07 1.25e-01

Thanks for the help. Happy holidays,
-ph

_________________
Philip DeWitt
Wildlife Ecologist
Ontario, Canada

covmat <- solve(out_test@opt$hessian)
